title: Pattern Committee: Contribution & Deprecation Playbook
creator: Sophie Chen
description:
Purpose: Establish a lightweight, predictable governance process for contributions to Redwood's design system (tokens, buttons, tables, charts, layout primitives) so changes are high-quality, easy to review, and reversible. This playbook defines the contribution flow, a review checklist for design + engineering, an RFC template for larger changes, and a clear deprecation policy for retiring tokens/components.

Scope: All design assets and code housed in packages/ui (tokens, components), figma libraries under 'Redwood DS', and ancillary docs (README, migration guides). Not in scope: one-off product UI experiments or vendor-provided components.

Contribution flow (summary):
1) Small tweak / bugfix (e.g., token value correction, button padding fix): submit a GitHub branch + PR titled [DES-CONTRIB] short summary, link the Figma frame if relevant, include visual diffs (chromatic or storybook snapshot). Add the label "ds-sm".
2) Component enhancement (behavioral/API change): open a short RFC (see RFC template) in design/notes or the DS RFC board, gain informal alignment in the weekly Pattern Committee sync, then implement with PR linking the RFC. Add labels: "ds-feature", "needs-eng-review".
3) Breaking change / token rename / visual redesign: mandatory RFC, designated migration plan, opt-in feature flag if applicable, and a 4-week deprecation runway.

Review checklist (authors should ensure these are addressed before requesting review):
- Design: provide Figma frames with Variant table, accessibility notes, and token mapping. Include visual snapshots at three breakpoints and a short rationale for visual changes.
- Engineering: include Storybook stories, unit/visual tests, migration helper (codemod or compatibility layer) if removing/renaming tokens, and performance notes for complex components (tables, charts).
- Accessibility: include keyboard/aria behavior, contrast checks, and screenreader sample text where applicable.
- Backwards compatibility: document expected consumer impact and roll-out strategy (feature flag, opt-in).
- Metrics & telemetry: if change affects rendering or data payloads (charts, table cell renderers), propose one metric to track (e.g., mean render time, error rate).
- Docs: update README, changelog entry, and migration guide snippets.

RFC process (lightweight):
- When to RFC: API surface changes, token naming changes, component contract changes, or new cross-product patterns.
- RFC template (summary): title, author, status (Draft / Ready / Accepted), motivation, alternatives considered, proposed API/manifest, migration plan, risks, rollout plan, acceptance criteria, timeline. Keep RFC under 1-2 pages.
- Review cadence: post RFC to /design-ds channel and Pattern Committee board; collect feedback for 7 business days. If no major objections, Committee votes (thumbs up/down) in weekly meeting. A tie requires escalation to Head of Design + Engineering manager.

Deprecation policy (practical steps):
1) Announce deprecation in the DS changelog and internal channel with a proposed removal date and migration guide.
2) Provide automated migration tools for token renames where feasible (codemod or mapping table).
3) Maintain deprecated token/component with warnings for at least 4 weeks (console warning or runtime warning in dev builds).
4) Schedule removal in the next minor release after the deprecation period; update deprecation notes in release docs.

Ownership & operating rhythm:
- Pattern Committee (rotating roster of 4: 2 designers, 2 FE engineers) owns approvals, meets weekly. Committee roster lives in the DS handbook in Drive.
- Triage channel: #ds-patterns for quick alignment; create RFCs for non-trivial changes.
- Quarterly review: audit tokens and components for duplication, unused tokens, and chart/table perf hotspots. Outcome posted to the Design System roadmap.

Acceptance criteria for merging major DS changes (authors must include this in PR):
- PR passes CI (unit and visual tests) and Storybook checks.
- Design sign-off comment in PR with a Figma link.
- Engineering sign-off with migration notes or compatibility layer.
- Accessibility checklist passed (or documented exemptions).
- Changelog and migration guide attached.

Why this matters: The DS surface is shared across multiple products and teams; small inconsistent changes accumulate into technical debt, increased developer friction, and UX regressions. This playbook keeps contributions predictable, reviewable, and reversible while enabling teams to move quickly.

Next steps: Share this draft with Pattern Committee on 2026-03-16 meeting; publish canonical doc in Drive under 'Design System / Governance' after iteration.

Links and artifacts: Figma library: https://drive.google.com/redwood/figma-ds (placeholder), DS RFC board: https://linear.app/redwood/board/ds-rfcs, Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/packages-ui/pull/1423, Codemod sketch: https://gist.github.com/redwood/codemod-token-rename
comments: 2026-03-10 Sophie Chen: Initial draft posted; focused on minimizing process friction while ensuring key checkpoints for tokens, buttons, tables, and charts.
2026-03-11 Marco Rivera: Added engineering checklist items (storybook, visual tests, migration helpers). Requested an example codemod link — added placeholder.
2026-03-12 Priya Nair (Accessibility): Reviewed checklist; requested explicit contrast checks for chart color palettes and aria-label patterns for table sorting. Marked as included.

2026-03-13 Josh Patel (Product): Suggested a shorter RFC window for urgent security fixes; Committee decided to allow 48-hour expedited review for security or accessibility-critical changes with post-hoc RFC documentation.
2026-03-14 Marco Rivera: Updated acceptance criteria to require design sign-off and added quarterly audit cadence. Preparing to present at Pattern Committee 2026-03-16.
